verdict.root_cause: productcatalogservice is failing a small, intermittent fraction of its own GetProduct calls. Its error ratio was exactly zero across a 968-sample four-hour baseline, then went non-zero from ~09:52 with a renewed burst at ~13:25 just before the alert [tr_3ee81acb3a6c]. The single sampled error trace puts the error on productcatalogservice's own GetProduct server span, failing in ~0.8ms with ~0.1ms self time, whose only child (FeatureFlagService/GetFlag) is fast and error-free, propagating up through checkoutservice/PlaceOrder to the frontend POST [tr_315c533aff54]. No deploy, image, tag, or config push exists anywhere in the window, and the only recorded activity (a 300ms egress delay injected and removed between 06:00 and 06:09) was net-zero and gone 7.3h before onset [tr_030d4296340e]. A fast in-handler rejection immediately after a feature-flag read, with no latency or saturation anywhere in the path, points to a flag-gated failure mode being enabled in productcatalogservice: the flag value is itself what makes the request fail. Downstream services are not the source - checkout still completes full order flows with successful payments and queue writes [tr_03699d01be59], and frontend's error ratio fell to 0.14x of its own baseline [tr_61ed613becc4], so the frontend alert is propagation, not an independent fault.
verdict.reasoning: Localization is solid: the only error span in the sample is productcatalogservice's own GetProduct handler, its one downstream call is clean and fast, and the failure is sub-millisecond rather than a timeout, excluding dependency latency and saturation [tr_315c533aff54]. The metric baseline shows the errors are new rather than a chronic floor and began hours before the alert, so nothing at 13:27 is the trigger [tr_3ee81acb3a6c]. Change history covers the full window with no deploy or image mutation, which is why this is not bad_deploy, and the delay injection was reverted long before onset [tr_030d4296340e]. Sparse, bursty, fast failures in a handler that reads a feature flag right before failing are the signature of an enabled failure flag, and a flag value whose wrongness is what breaks the request is bad_config, remediated by reverting it. Confidence is low: the flag state was never read, and the productcatalogservice log query returned nothing under a selector its own specialist judged a probable label mismatch [tr_44cf857d8e4e], so the mechanism rests on one error trace out of 150 spans.
open_questions: The feature flag state was never queried; the flag-gated mechanism is inferred from trace shape alone and is unconfirmed.
productcatalogservice's own logs were never really read - the selector likely mismatched the label, so error returns, panics and restarts remain unexamined; re-querying is the top next step.
What started the errors at ~09:52 is unexplained, and whether the failures are scoped by product id, caller, or fixed probability cannot be told from one error trace.

alternatives.root_cause: An internal code defect or bad catalog data in productcatalogservice makes a subset of GetProduct calls fail, with no configuration value involved.
alternatives.why_not: Fits the trace shape equally well but explains nothing about onset timing and offers no actionable fix; the flag read immediately preceding the failing return gives the config reading a concrete mechanism this lacks.

alternatives.root_cause: Residual or re-applied traffic-shaping/network interference on productcatalogservice's namespace degrades a fraction of its RPCs.
alternatives.why_not: The injection was removed with the delay parameter reverted 7.3h before onset [tr_030d4296340e], and every sampled span including the erroring one completes in under ~1ms, so no wait is occurring [tr_315c533aff54].

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so nothing should change: productcatalogservice's error ratio should continue to show the same sparse, bursty pattern (window mean ~0.5%, peaks ~12%, most 2m scrapes at exactly 0) against a 968-sample baseline of exactly zero [tr_3ee81acb3a6c], and errors should continue to appear as sub-millisecond failures on its own GetProduct server span [tr_315c533aff54]. The observable next step is diagnostic, not remedial: re-run the Loki query with a corrected label value (the hyphenated selector {service="product-catalog-service"} returned zero lines over a 32-minute window that fully spans the burst, plausibly a label mismatch [tr_44cf857d8e4e]) and query the actual FeatureFlagService flag state for the GetProduct path. Success of that step is measured by non-empty log output naming an error return or rejection reason, and by a concrete flag value with an enable timestamp that can be compared against the 09:52:30 onset.
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the flag query comes back showing a productcatalogservice-scoped flag that was enabled at or before 09:52:30, or if change history re-queried against the right identifier turns up a config push / flag mutation and a recorded prior configuration for this service. Either of those would satisfy revert_config's preconditions and make a targeted config revert the correct proposal, at the cost of the extra minutes spent confirming. It is also wrong if the errors escalate from the current ~0.5% mean into a sustained elevation and start showing up as failed PlaceOrder flows in checkoutservice logs, which currently complete end to end with successful payments and advancing queue offsets [tr_03699d01be59] - in that case waiting for confirmation becomes more expensive than acting on a low-confidence diagnosis.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued customer-visible checkout failures at the current low rate for as long as diagnosis takes; the error condition has already run ~3.5 hours since 09:52:30 [tr_3ee81acb3a6c] so the marginal cost of another few minutes is small but not zero. The risk of the alternative - proposing revert_config anyway - is larger: change history covering the full window records no deploy, no config push, and no image or tag change for productcatalogservice, only a matched, net-zero traffic-shaping attach/detach pair 7.3h before onset [tr_030d4296340e]. With no prior configuration recorded, a revert would restore an unknown or default environment, could repoint dependency addresses that are currently correct, and would recreate the container - discarding cache and resetting the very process state needed to reproduce and diagnose an intermittent 0.5% failure. It would also destroy the evidence trail while leaving the real trigger, which is unexplained at 09:52, in place. The flag-gated mechanism is inferred from the shape of one sampled error trace and has never been confirmed by querying flag state.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because no change is made. Had an action been taken on productcatalogservice, the container recreate would reset connections for its three named callers: checkoutservice (the only path carrying the error span, via PlaceOrder), frontend (GetProduct on product pages, currently clean), and recommendationservice (ListProducts, currently clean at ~0.0ms) [tr_315c533aff54] - meaning two currently healthy call paths would be disturbed to chase a fault visible on one. The diagnostic re-queries proposed instead are read-only against Loki, Tempo and the flag store and are visible to no service.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical multi-service alerting starting at productcatalogservice and propagating to frontend and load generator is not dismissible. Pattern fits a productcatalogservice degradation fanning out to its consumers, though a recent deploy or resource limit there is equally plausible.
